opportunities.problem: Select KV state under a fixed memory budget while preserving generation quality over future queries.
opportunities.baseline_guarantee_or_result: The papers report substantial cache reduction with task-dependent retained quality; no universal exact semantic guarantee is claimed for lossy eviction.
opportunities.limitation_or_gap: Future-query utility is unknown at eviction time; robustness across a query family is not generally certified.
opportunities.workload_relevance: Long-context and reasoning requests make KV memory and attention cost operational bottlenecks.
opportunities.potential_improvement: Reduce catastrophic quality loss across multiple future queries at equal retained bytes.

mechanism.input: KV entries, layer/head identity, fixed cache budget, declared future-query family or uncertainty model
mechanism.state: Per-entry importance estimate and lower-confidence utility score by layer
mechanism.operation: Admit/evict entries by a robust lower-confidence utility-per-byte rule subject to protected mandatory positions
mechanism.correctness: Cache budget must be respected; quality remains approximate and requires an explicit error endpoint
mechanism.cost: Scoring and metadata overhead plus bytes retained and downstream attention cost
mechanism.failure_case: An adversarial future query depends on a token receiving low score under the observed prompt/query
mechanism.novelty_hypothesis: Potentially distinct only if a nontrivial distributionally robust guarantee survives comparison with KVzip and query-aware eviction; unverified

opportunities.success_measure: At fixed retained bytes, improve worst-group or lower-quantile task quality without increasing end-to-end memory traffic enough to erase throughput.
opportunities.fastest_falsifier: Construct multi-query cases where the required evidence is in low-score cache positions; compare at exactly matched bytes and full inference cost.
opportunities.implementation_risk: high; model-specific kernels, GPU memory layout, quality and latency coupling

opportunities.problem: Choose a draft-token tree maximizing end-to-end decode speed subject to target verification and drafting cost.
strongest_baselines: Sequoia dynamic-programming tree optimizer and hardware-aware sizing
opportunities.baseline_guarantee_or_result: Sequoia optimizes tree structures under its model; OPT-Tree optimizes expected acceptance length; SMART directly uses hardware-aware marginal benefit/cost for end-to-end speedup.
opportunities.limitation_or_gap: Potential residual question is cross-request queueing externality, but no source-supported gap distinct from serving schedulers was established.
opportunities.workload_relevance: Speculative decoding reduces serial target-model steps but tree verification and drafting can become costly at batch scale.
opportunities.potential_improvement: Improve aggregate goodput under contention without changing target output distribution.

mechanism.input: Draft/target token distributions, tree prefix state, measured marginal compute, batch load and SLO slack
mechanism.state: Candidate tree frontier and per-request marginal verified-token benefit/cost estimates
mechanism.operation: Expand a node only if its marginal aggregate-goodput gain exceeds its marginal target/draft and queueing cost
mechanism.correctness: Must preserve target sampling distribution under the speculative acceptance rule
mechanism.cost: Target forward, draft forward, tree memory, batching and scheduling overhead
mechanism.failure_case: Two requests compete for a saturated target batch and local gain displaces a request with higher global value
mechanism.novelty_hypothesis: Weak; SMART already contributes runtime marginal hardware benefit-cost tree growth

opportunities.success_measure: Higher tokens/sec or SLO goodput at identical output distribution, hardware, batch arrivals and total target/draft FLOPs.
opportunities.fastest_falsifier: Small two-request contention trace comparing local and aggregate decisions under measured tree costs.
opportunities.implementation_risk: high; runtime scheduler and target-model GPU instrumentation required

opportunities.problem: Route prompt-prefill and decode work across resources while optimizing prefix reuse, latency, and SLO goodput.
strongest_baselines: TaiChi hybrid prefill/decode aggregation-disaggregation with latency shifting
ARES adaptive decode rescheduling from output-length prediction
opportunities.baseline_guarantee_or_result: Source papers report workload-specific latency/goodput improvements; these are paper-reported and not reproduced here.
opportunities.limitation_or_gap: A new scheduler must distinguish itself from adaptive rescheduling and SLO-aware hybrid placement; no narrower open gap was isolated.
opportunities.workload_relevance: Multi-tenant LLM services face heterogeneous prompt lengths, output lengths, cache locality, TTFT and TPOT constraints.
opportunities.potential_improvement: Reduce tail SLO violations and increase SLO-satisfied requests on the same cluster.

mechanism.input: Arrival stream, prefix-cache metadata, TTFT/TPOT deadlines, calibrated residual-length intervals, GPU capacity
mechanism.state: Per-request slack, resource queue forecasts, cache-location and migration-cost metadata
mechanism.operation: Assign or migrate request only when robust predicted SLO-goodput gain exceeds transfer and interference costs
mechanism.correctness: No request loss; preserve model output semantics and declared SLO accounting
mechanism.cost: GPU time, KV transfer, cache duplication, migration stalls, predictor computation
mechanism.failure_case: Heavy-tailed outputs and miscalibrated intervals trigger migrations or overload the decode pool
mechanism.novelty_hypothesis: Unclear given TaiChi and ARES; no theorem or unique mechanism identified

opportunities.success_measure: Higher SLO-satisfied goodput and lower p99 TTFT/TPOT on matched hardware and arrival traces, including transfer costs.
opportunities.fastest_falsifier: Replay a heavy-tailed output trace with adversarially biased length predictions and account for migrations.
opportunities.implementation_risk: very_high; multi-GPU cluster, traces and serving engine needed

opportunities.problem: Select retrieval strategy and context size per query to trade evidence coverage, answer quality and cost.
strongest_baselines: MBA-RAG contextual bandit over retrieval strategies
opportunities.baseline_guarantee_or_result: Published results are benchmark-specific; Adaptive-k is single-pass thresholding and MBA-RAG explicitly reward-penalizes retrieval cost.
opportunities.limitation_or_gap: The key missing object is a calibrated, portable probability that a chosen context covers the answer evidence.
opportunities.workload_relevance: Context length directly affects retrieval work, prompt cost and answer support.
opportunities.potential_improvement: Meet a declared evidence-coverage risk target at lower retrieval/generation cost.

mechanism.input: Query, candidate passages, similarity/relevance scores, cost per retrieval action, calibration set
mechanism.state: Per-action coverage calibrator and uncertainty interval
mechanism.operation: Choose the cheapest action whose lower confidence bound on coverage exceeds risk threshold; otherwise abstain or escalate
mechanism.output: Selected passages, retrieval plan, or escalation
mechanism.correctness: No false claim of coverage; preserve provenance from selected evidence to answer
mechanism.cost: Retrieval calls, reranker/model calls, tokens and calibration overhead
mechanism.failure_case: Distribution shift or multi-hop aggregation yields confidently omitted evidence
mechanism.novelty_hypothesis: May reduce to selective prediction/contextual bandits; no distinct guarantee established

opportunities.success_measure: Lower token/retrieval cost at fixed answer/evidence error, or improved support at matched total cost.
opportunities.fastest_falsifier: Out-of-domain multi-hop queries where the top-k similarity distribution is confidently misleading.
opportunities.implementation_risk: high; QA labels, retrieval corpus and model inference required

opportunities.area: database algorithms and dynamic query processing
opportunities.problem: Maintain exact conjunctive-query output under single-tuple insertions/deletions with constant-delay enumeration and low update cost.
strongest_baselines: 2026 PODS heavy-light partitioning with delta queries and materialized-view trees
opportunities.baseline_guarantee_or_result: The official record identifies a generic heavy-light incremental-maintenance algorithm for arbitrary join queries. An accessible paper-text mirror describes maintenance width and threshold optimization, but the ACM primary PDF returned HTTP 403, so the detailed theorem and optimization scope were not independently reconstructed.
opportunities.limitation_or_gap: Primary full-text access was blocked in this session; it is therefore unknown whether online threshold adaptation under changing skew is outside the paper's threshold optimization or adjacent update-dependent work.
opportunities.workload_relevance: Heavy key skew can make one static decomposition expensive under evolving data distributions.
opportunities.potential_improvement: Bound total update plus migration work against a causal fixed threshold while preserving exact constant-delay output.

mechanism.input: Fixed query hypergraph, tuple-update stream, relation/key frequencies, threshold portfolio of powers of two
mechanism.state: Active exact delta views, heavy/light partitions, versioned migration progress, skew summaries
mechanism.operation: Switch with hysteresis only when predicted width savings over a bounded horizon exceed exact view migration cost; publish new view atomically
mechanism.output: Exact query answers continuously, enumerated with declared delay after committed updates
mechanism.correctness: Exact answers throughout reclassification; prove no missing or double-counted tuples across versions
mechanism.cost: Update, view migration, storage duplication, enumeration delay, synchronization
mechanism.failure_case: A key frequency alternates just around the switching threshold, causing view-migration thrashing
mechanism.novelty_hypothesis: Potentially meaningful but unverified; the accessible mirror reports threshold minimization, but exact theorem scope was not verified from the primary full text

opportunities.success_measure: A proven amortized total-cost bound versus the best causal static threshold, with exact answers and constant-delay enumeration; any empirical study must include migration and storage.
opportunities.fastest_falsifier: Two-relation join with a key's frequency oscillating around threshold then shifting persistently; charge every rebuild and check delay/exactness.
opportunities.implementation_risk: medium_to_high; maintaining multiple exact view portfolios can multiply storage and write cost
opportunities.source_access: Official DOI/PODS record and abstract checked; ACM PDF endpoint returned HTTP 403. Detailed maintenance-width notes are provisional secondary-access observations, not independently authenticated theorem details.

opportunities.problem: Trade vector-index memory and distance-computation cost against approximate-neighbor recall under data changes.
strongest_baselines: RaBitQ unbiased estimator with theoretical error bound
opportunities.baseline_guarantee_or_result: RaBitQ gives a data-independent estimator error analysis; the extension covers higher-accuracy space/error tradeoffs and reports real-dataset results.
opportunities.limitation_or_gap: Dynamic insertion/deletion and codebook rebuild costs were not source-audited enough to establish a novel open problem.
opportunities.workload_relevance: ANN is a core operator in vector search and retrieval systems; index bytes and recall jointly matter.
opportunities.potential_improvement: Maintain accuracy guarantees while reducing update/rebuild amplification under drifting data.

mechanism.input: Vector stream, query workload, recall/error target, update-rate budget
mechanism.state: Quantization codebook, residual/error certificates, generation-tagged vector codes
mechanism.operation: Use an immutable base codebook plus bounded delta codes; compact only when certified residual mass exceeds a threshold
mechanism.output: Neighbor candidates with a stated approximation/recall guarantee
mechanism.correctness: Preserve the ANN guarantee across base-plus-delta search and compaction
mechanism.cost: Index bytes, query scans, delta overhead, compaction CPU and write amplification
mechanism.failure_case: Distribution drift invalidates residual error bounds before compaction or delta scan overwhelms query latency
mechanism.novelty_hypothesis: Unverified; resembles standard LSM-style indexing plus quantization and needs a precise transfer theorem

opportunities.success_measure: At matched recall, lower total bytes plus query and update cost over a frozen update/query sequence.
opportunities.fastest_falsifier: Adversarial distribution shift that maximizes residual norm and forces frequent compactions.
opportunities.implementation_risk: high; requires ANN datasets, index engineering and matched recall tuning

opportunities.problem: Maintain approximate vertex cover or matching in geometric intersection graphs under object updates.
strongest_baselines: Bhore-Chan fully dynamic geometric MVC/MCM frameworks
opportunities.baseline_guarantee_or_result: For several geometric classes the source gives polylog amortized update-time approximation schemes, including near-(1+epsilon) factors for disks/hypercubes and 3/2+epsilon cover for planar rectangles.
opportunities.limitation_or_gap: This screen did not isolate a family where worst-case update time, deterministic behavior, and the same approximation factor are both open and not implied by the source framework.
opportunities.workload_relevance: Dynamic geometric conflict/overlap graphs arise in spatial resource allocation.
opportunities.potential_improvement: Deamortize update latency while retaining approximation and compact state.

mechanism.input: Geometric object insert/delete stream, fixed dimension and epsilon
mechanism.state: Approximate primal solution, local certificates and a background rebuild structure
mechanism.operation: Spread rebuild work over future updates and use local repair certificates before publishing a new solution
mechanism.output: A maintained approximate cover or matching
mechanism.correctness: Every update leaves a valid solution with a proved approximation factor
mechanism.cost: Worst-case update time, space, rebuild backlog and approximation loss
mechanism.failure_case: Adversarial update burst outruns background rebuild or destroys the local certificate
mechanism.novelty_hypothesis: Likely standard deamortization unless a new structural certificate is found

opportunities.success_measure: Worst-case rather than amortized update guarantee at a fixed approximation and space bound.
opportunities.fastest_falsifier: Burst sequence that consumes rebuild slack; prove or measure whether approximation validity breaks.
opportunities.implementation_risk: medium; geometric data structures and worst-case instrumentation needed

opportunities.problem: Estimate SQL plan cardinalities under workload distribution shift while preserving plan quality.
opportunities.baseline_guarantee_or_result: CardOOD reports improvements across OOD settings and an integration into PostgreSQL; results are empirical, not a worst-case optimizer guarantee.
opportunities.limitation_or_gap: The source already directly encodes partial-order constraints; this screen did not identify a new invariant beyond that idea.
opportunities.workload_relevance: Cardinality errors can cause poor join plans and large runtime regressions.
opportunities.potential_improvement: Use runtime feedback to improve robust estimation under query/data shift without harmful model updates.

mechanism.input: Query predicates, schema/statistics, observed cardinalities from completed operators
mechanism.state: Calibrated estimator plus monotonicity constraints for nested query predicates
mechanism.operation: Apply bounded online correction from feedback while projecting predictions onto only semantically valid order constraints
mechanism.output: Cardinality estimates consumed by cost-based optimizer
mechanism.correctness: No false semantic constraints; SQL NULLs, joins and correlations must be handled
mechanism.cost: Feedback storage, update latency, estimator inference and plan search effects
mechanism.failure_case: Correlated predicates or non-nested query shapes make imposed monotonic constraints mislead plan costing
mechanism.novelty_hypothesis: Weak; the central partial-order mechanism is already present in CardOOD

opportunities.success_measure: Lower workload runtime regret under held-out distribution shifts with identical optimization time and no semantic constraint violations.
opportunities.fastest_falsifier: Correlated predicate workload where online monotone projection increases q-error or plan runtime.
opportunities.implementation_risk: high; DBMS integration, workload suite and optimizer reproducibility required
